entries: See the occupational profile for the shared criteria.

paragraphs: If you prefer maintaining accurate, continuous financial records over the long term, consider corporate accounting first. If you prefer spotting anomalies in evidence and independently assessing reliability, consider auditing first. If interpreting regulations and filing compliance interest you more, consider tax. If you focus more on budgets, forecasts and operating decisions, consider financial analysis. Movement between roles is possible, but their required regulatory knowledge, systems skills, audit methods and business analysis skills are not identical.

Accounting, auditing, tax and financial analysis all handle corporate financial information, but their core tasks, outputs and responsibilities differ. Accounting records and prepares financial information; auditing independently verifies its reliability; tax focuses on filing and compliance; financial analysis focuses on budgets, forecasts and operating decisions. When choosing a direction, compare whether you prefer building records, verifying evidence, interpreting rules or forecasting the future.
More focused on recording and basic checks; accountants also undertake closing, statement preparation, analysis and compliance judgments.
Want to start with basic finance processes and build experience in accounting and system operations.
Enter transactions, classify vouchers and check basic accounts to produce complete records for accounting treatment.
Corporate accountants establish and interpret financial records; auditors independently examine whether those records and controls are reliable.
Enjoy continuously maintaining accounting systems and completing closing and statements on a regular cycle.
Handle closing, the general ledger, financial statements, cost accounting and internal control documentation.
Does not involve keeping the client's books; the core is independent verification, professional scepticism and evidence evaluation.
Enjoy investigating anomalies and verifying evidence, and can accept engagement-based work and concentrated deadlines.
Examine financial statements, obtain audit evidence, assess risks of material misstatement and form an audit opinion.
Serves internal organisational governance, covering operations, compliance and risk, not only financial statements.
More interested in processes, risk, compliance and cross-departmental communication.
Evaluate internal controls, risk management and business processes, and recommend improvements.
Relies more on tax law and filing rules; accounting and auditing cover a broader range of financial information and controls.
Enjoy studying regulations and dealing with explicit rules and filing deadlines.
Carry out tax filings, tax accounting, policy interpretation and compliant tax planning.
Accounting mainly explains transactions that have already occurred; financial analysis focuses more on future operating results.
Enjoy modelling, forecasting, business analysis and explaining data to management.
Prepare budgets, forecast operating results, analyse variances and support management decisions.
After identifying a career direction, you also need to assess which tasks are being automated and which professional judgments and responsibilities must still be handled by people.
May 2025 OEWS covers U.S. wage and salary workers. The self-employed are outside the survey scope. May 2025 national medians: Accountants and auditors (13-2011): $83,680/year.

O*NET lists the interest code for accountants and auditors (13-2011.00) as CEI: Conventional C comes first, followed by Enterprising E and Investigative I. This indicates that the occupational environment usually emphasises orderly records and rule application, alongside analytical investigation and communication to influence others. It describes occupational tasks, not a personal qualifying threshold.

Editorial observation: resolving inconsistencies between vouchers, payment records and books and producing a reviewable explanation of differences may provide a sense of task completion. Whether you enjoy this repeated verification should be tested through practical exercises and experience in a role.
Conventional C, Enterprising E and Investigative I; describes the occupational environment, not an ability or qualification threshold.

entries: Conventional interests: willingness to organise complete records according to standards, processes and evidence.
Investigative and Enterprising interests: willingness to investigate differences, form judgments and explain conclusions to relevant people.

paragraphs: CEI is an occupational profile, not a personal pass code. Other interest combinations may also suit a specific accounting direction; verify this against real tasks.

The Big Five describes personality with continuous dimensions. A synthesis of 54 meta-analyses reports an average conscientiousness association of about ρ=.19 with overall performance, with modest effects varying by performance category. As an editorial suggestion, reflect on habits such as accurate records, planning, review and deadline management; this is not an accounting-specific prediction, competence threshold or validation of this site’s assessment.

entries: Higher conscientiousness usually supports detailed checks, planned execution and timely completion.
Lower emotional volatility helps in handling corrections and busy seasons; openness helps in learning new standards and systems, but its role depends on the job.

paragraphs: Personality and performance have probabilistic associations, not causal conclusions or hiring cutoffs. Ability, training, experience, control processes and team environment also matter.

Official Myers-Briggs career guidance states that preferences do not determine abilities, skills or competencies and that the assessment is not designed for hiring or job selection. This page uses no MBTI type as a condition for hiring, excluding or assigning someone to an accounting or auditing role. Reflect on information-processing, decision-making and collaboration preferences, then explore actual requirements through programs and task materials.

entries: Observe preferences: which is less draining for you—structured processes or open exploration, independent analysis or frequent collaboration?
Compare preferences separately against general ledger, audit, tax, FP&A, forensic accounting or management roles rather than focusing only on four letters.

paragraphs: This page uses no MBTI type for hiring or excluding a career. Relevant knowledge, skills and task evidence are needed to assess role competence.

There is currently no reliable evidence that a particular Enneagram number is better suited to accounting. A systematic review of 104 independent samples found mixed evidence for Enneagram reliability and validity, with limited support for core claims such as "nine types", wings and movement between types. It can therefore serve only as a self-reflection tool for motivation and stress patterns.

entries: Observe whether accuracy, control, security, achievement, knowledge-seeking or service motivates you most.
Identify whether month-end closing, audit or tax deadlines trigger perfectionism, avoidance, anxiety or rash action in you.

paragraphs: Do not create or trust "best number rankings". The Enneagram cannot establish occupational competence or replace validated ability and work sample assessments.

This page sets no accounting or audit entry threshold using an IQ score. Start with rule comprehension, numerical comparison, anomaly identification and explaining judgments in specific tasks. BLS describes numerical-analysis requirements; ACCA discusses basic arithmetic, percentages, ratios, estimation and spreadsheet formulas in much accounting study, with more advanced mathematics in some financial or quantitative directions.

entries: Can understand rules, check assumptions, compare numbers and clearly explain the reasoning process.
Willing to review calculations, investigate unexpected differences and build specific skills through courses and tools.

paragraphs: Do not rule yourself out based on a single IQ score. Course performance, practical tasks, learning speed and the mathematical depth required by the role tell you more about fit than an abstract label.

Translate communication requirements into observable behavior: listen to questions, discuss facts, explain findings and request information clearly from colleagues or clients. BLS explicitly describes these communication skills. This page uses no EQ score to determine accounting or audit qualifications and treats no general communication exercise as validation of this site’s assessment.

entries: Can uphold principles and avoid unnecessary conflict when requesting missing evidence or pointing out control problems.
Can listen to the business context and translate technical conclusions into actions clients, management and teams can take.

paragraphs: Assessments here support reflection only. Check communication, professional knowledge, independence, skepticism and ethical responsibilities separately; one score replaces none of these.

Corporate accounting / general ledger tasks emphasise stable cycles, complete records and responsibility for month-end closing. The bookkeeping clerks below are included only to compare basic recordkeeping tasks and are not equivalent to a full accountant role.
Repetitive tasks, concentrated closing deadlines and continually following up on missing original vouchers.

External auditing emphasises evidence, professional scepticism, client communication and engagement teamwork. The financial examiners below provide a comparison with related regulatory tasks, not a synonymous occupation for external auditing.
Busy-season hours, travel, client resistance and multiple rounds of review of your work.
Enjoy reading rules, tracking exceptions, documenting positions and managing hard deadlines.
Continually changing regulations, filing peaks and consequences of inaccurate interpretation.
Enjoy analysis, business contexts, forecasting, communication and influencing operating decisions.

The link leads to financial and investment analysts for comparison of related analytical tasks, not an equivalent corporate management-accounting or FP&A role. Check specific duties, education and recruitment conditions separately.
Enjoy anomaly detection, evidence chains, investigation, scepticism and defensible conclusions.
Conflict, incomplete information, sensitive cases and rigorous written documentation.
Want to combine controls, systems, judgment, team leadership and communication with senior management.
Responsibility expands from technical accuracy to people, priorities, risks and organisational trust.
Can organise evidence, identify inconsistencies, complete repeated reviews and explain the business meaning behind numbers.
If you consistently avoid rules, documentation, review by others, concentrated deadlines or difficult follow-up questions, this work may be particularly draining.

Check the  reimbursement documents on this page, document amount differences, missing materials and review recommendations, and record checking accuracy and energy levels. One exercise cannot represent complete role competence.

rows: Finance / accounting assistant

Organise vouchers and attachments, assist with data entry, expense review, basic reconciliation and preparation of month-end closing materials; the organisation determines the specific scope of authorisation.
Can match transactions, vouchers and records, flag and follow up on missing documents, and produce work files that others can review.
Submit a one-page reconciliation note covering supporting records, any difference and the next review step.
Closest to entering everyday accounting, starting with building records; unlike audit assistance, independent verification of evidence is not the core.
Accounts receivable, accounts payable or expense accountant
Check invoices, receipts and payments, receivable/payable balances and expense documents, follow up on open items and assist with closing.
Can organise details in Excel, locate differences, explain ageing or open items, and retain supporting reasons for actions taken.
Submit a receivables/payables reconciliation, a list of reasons for differences and proposed corrections.
More focused on specific cycles and frequent checks; a common starting point for general ledger or shared services.
Audit assistant
Perform sampling or testing procedures under engagement team guidance, request and organise evidence, prepare working papers and follow up on review comments.
Procedures align with risks, evidence is indexed, anomalies are escalated, and working paper conclusions match attachments.
Submit a simplified audit working paper: objective, procedures, sample, anomalies, evidence index and conclusion.
Focuses on independent verification and evidence sufficiency, usually with stronger engagement-based work, client communication and concentrated deadline pressure.
Internal audit assistant / inspection assistant
Understand business processes and assist with control testing, document verification, issue recording and follow-up on remediation.
Can connect processes, risks, controls, evidence and findings, and distinguish facts, judgments and recommendations.
Submit a procure-to-pay flowchart, three control tests and an issue tracking sheet.
Focuses on internal organisational governance and process improvement, covering operations and compliance, not only financial statements.
Tax assistant
Organise filing documents and transaction information, and assist with basic tax calculations, form preparation, policy retrieval and deadline management.
Can locate applicable rules, reconcile filing data with accounting records, and clearly document assumptions and matters awaiting confirmation.
Submit a filing-document checklist using training records, a regulatory source log and a note explaining any differences.
Relies more on tax law, filing rules and timing; complex transactions and final filing responsibility require review by experienced staff.

items.title: What work samples can you create without experience?

values: Day 1 | Choose an entry point
Compare corporate accounting, external auditing and internal auditing, choose one direction, and write down two questions you want to test.
Day 2 | Read the materials
List the ledger balance and the two supporting figures separately. Write down the account and period they share.
Day 3 | Complete the checks
Compare amounts one by one, calculate the difference and cite the document sources; do not invent explanations for missing information.
Day 4 | Follow up on documents
Identify which original posting or supporting document would help explain the mismatch and write a one-sentence request.
Day 5 | Prepare a note
Organise facts, evidence gaps and review recommendations on one page; keep questions with no new documents marked as awaiting confirmation.
Day 6 | Check against the reference
Compare your result with the worked answer. Check the direction of the difference and whether the conclusion stays within the evidence.
Day 7 | Revise and decide
Submit a second version, compare errors, time spent and energy levels, then decide which direction to test further or temporarily rule out.
